question: Should the shared `agent-transcript` skill accept GitHub Copilot session discovery as a supported public-transcript source under this PR’s fail-closed allowlist and redaction contract?
rationale: The code adds a new local source whose output may be inserted into public GitHub bodies; tests can reduce implementation risk but cannot choose the acceptable privacy and support boundary.

options.title: Approve Copilot support with current-head proof
options.body: Accept Copilot as a supported source, contingent on a current-head redacted live render and repository validation confirming the documented allowlist/redaction contract.

options.title: Keep source support narrower
options.body: Limit the skill to existing session formats until maintainers define a more general source-admission and privacy-review policy.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Do not merge this discovery path if maintainers do not want local Copilot session material considered for public provenance output.

recommendation.title: Approve Copilot support with current-head proof
recommendation.body: Accept Copilot as a supported source, contingent on a current-head redacted live render and repository validation confirming the documented allowlist/redaction contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed implementation and can supply the exact-head behavior evidence needed once the privacy boundary is chosen.
